dse_runs.notes: Bursty Poisson load: bursts of 8 requests 0 ns apart, 2 req/us mean; p99 latency <= 0.4 us. Pipelined families should handle bursts well; iterative designs risk p99 violations under burst load. Max error <= 2^-10, so accuracy_bits >= 10. Minimise LUTs+FFs.

final_text: Campaign complete. For the single spec **bursty_offload**, I spent the full 400-evaluation L1 budget on the structured DSE graph (refine → refine → stop), which produced a 47-design feasible Pareto front dominated by pipelined_m designs. L2 SimPy simulation of the top 5 confirmed all pass the p99 latency constraint (simulated p99 ≈ 0.195–0.233 µs vs the 0.4 µs limit — the L1 analytic bounds underestimated latency by ~25%), with the winner unchanged: **`pipelined_m:data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=1, frac_guard=1, rounding=trunc, m=6`** — 770 LUTs+FFs (estimated), 10.2 accuracy bits (max error 2^-10.23, within the 2^-10 limit), 68.5 MSps throughput. L3/L4 had no recorded data for this design (fresh verification too heavy, no recorded synthesis), so back_annotate returned no measured data and no winner change was flagged; no reexplore was needed. The spec was finalized on the L2-simulated selection.
